neighbours.label: Competing with or overtaking a rival ('compete with', 'have overtaken', 'outpaced', 'pull ahead of'), firing on the preposition or the verb's last piece; neutral relations between the same things stay quiet.
fire: Small shops cannot compete with the big chains.
Electric cars have overtaken diesel models in sales.
The young runner pulled ahead of the champion.
Weeds compete with crops for water.
Our city now rivals the capital for tourists.
The startup outpaced its older competitors.
Cuckoo chicks compete with the host's own chicks for food.
quiet: Small shops sell goods from the big chains.
Electric cars are parked next to diesel models.
The young runner trained with the champion.
Weeds grow among the crops near the water.
Streaming is offered alongside cable television.
Our city sits near the capital.
The startup hired its older staff.
Cuckoo chicks are fed by the host birds.

notes: Card: ' with' x9, ' over' x4, ' above' x2, ' behind' x2 (Labradoodles have actually overt⟦aken⟧ Poodles; metals may compete⟦ with⟧ ionized species). Exploratory probe: 'compete with calcium' 0.79, 'have overtaken Poodles' 0.74; 'bind calcium' 0.01.
